title: Warmly Spiced Tunisian Lamb Tagine
description: A quick and flavorful Tunisian dish featuring lamb, juniper berries, and a rich deglaze fond, this tagine is perfect for a weeknight dinner. It combines resinous and crumbly textures with a blend of warm spices.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in the bottom of a clay or ceramic tagine or a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the lamb cubes and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it starts to soften, about 3 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Stir in the crushed juniper berries, ground cumin, ground coriander, and cayenne pepper, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth, dried apricots, salt, and black pepper, and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the tagine or Dutch oven, and simmer, covered, for 1 1/2 hours, or until the lamb is tender.
Remove the tagine or Dutch oven from the heat and let it cool slightly before serving.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with fresh parsley or cilantro, if desired.
Cook poultry to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F before serving.
